vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/write/worked-example-produces-canonical-oml
vectors.comment: E.13's worked example in the write direction. Combined with extensions-osd-oml/parse/worked-example-round-trips-to-equivalent-osd, this establishes the E.13 round-trip requirement for this schema: parse_schema_oml(write_schema_oml(S)) == S, since write_schema_oml's output here is exactly parse_schema_oml's input there. The canonical writer emits records/fields in declaration order (Sec3.3's canonical serialization order invariant, principle 1 -- nothing merges here), omits `cardinality` for exactly-1 (E.5), and omits `nullable` unless true (E.6) -- this vector pins that exact formatting, not just equivalence, since it is the reference for what 'canonical' means for this extension.

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/write/exactly-one-cardinality-omits-the-edge
vectors.comment: E.5: the default cardinality (exactly 1, no OSD suffix) is written with the `cardinality` edge omitted entirely, not as `cardinality: {}`. Both are legal to read (E.5's table), but the writer picks one canonical spelling -- omission -- for the common case, the same way it omits `nullable` unless true (E.6).

vectors.name: extensions-osd-oml/write/any-type-has-no-name-edge
vectors.comment: E.6: `any` is written as `{ kind: "any" }` with no `name` edge -- `Type.name` is [0,1], absent for `any` (E.8's table).
